<system-reminder>
Codebase and user instructions are shown below. Be sure to adhere to these instructions. IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written.

Contents of /home/runner/work/codeReader/codeReader/work/openinfer-project-openinfer/CLAUDE.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

# AI-Assisted Contributions

AI-assisted PRs must be accountable and verifiable. Show that the work is not duplicated, name the production invariant being changed, and provide real evidence: production E2E for features and fixes, same-context A/B for performance, and model evals for output or accuracy changes. Every changed file must serve that invariant; remove unrelated cleanup, thin wrappers, generated scaffolding, and mock or source-text tests presented as production evidence.

# Team Documentation Workflow

Collaboration centered on the `docs/` directory.

## Knowledge Architecture (domain-axis)

Docs are organized by what they're *about*, not by lifecycle stage. A doc's freshness lives in its TL;DR (and `Last touched:` for active areas) — not by which directory it sits in. Completed work stays co-located with its domain. There is no `archives/` directory — if a doc no longer earns its keep, delete it; if a lasting lesson hides inside it, lift that lesson into `lessons/` first, then delete.

```
docs/
├── index.md           # Routing table — every doc must be listed here
├── roadmap/           # Strategic plans, quarterly direction, milestones
├── models/<line>/     # Per-model living docs (qwen3, qwen35, kimi-k2, ...)
│                      # — design, accuracy, perf, refactor records, gotchas
├── subsystems/<area>/ # Cross-cutting components (runtime, scheduler, frontend, kernels)
├── playbooks/         # Reusable how-to: benching, profiling, accuracy, onboarding
├── lessons/           # Tribal knowledge from research / other projects
├── benchmarks/        # Standalone benchmark snapshots and eval reports
├── conventions/       # Ongoing standards (bench regression, coding style)
└── private/           # Local-only notes (gitignored)
```

Classification rule at capture time:
- Is it tied to a specific model? → `models/<line>/`
- A specific subsystem? → `subsystems/<area>/`
- Reusable how-to applicable across models? → `playbooks/`
- Lasting lesson from elsewhere (other repo, research, postmortem)? → `lessons/`
- Snapshot of measurement, not a doc that evolves? → `benchmarks/`
- Strategic / cross-cutting plan? → `roadmap/`

If you can't pick one, the doc probably needs splitting.

## Documentation Style

- Docs cover what `--help` and code can't: pitfalls, diagnostic paths, decision context. Don't restate CLI reference.
- Every command in a doc must be run and verified before committing. Unverified commands are technical debt.
- The only required header is a one-line **TL;DR**. Keep it true; that's the contract.
- For `models/<line>/` and `subsystems/<area>/` docs, add `Last touched: YYYY-MM` and bump it when you do meaningful work on the doc (not for typo fixes). The date is a fact, not a judgement — readers infer freshness themselves.
- `playbooks/`, `lessons/`, `conventions/`, `roadmap/`, `benchmarks/`, `archives/` don't need a freshness stamp. They're either timeless until disproven, or self-dated, or explicitly inert.
- No `Status:` enum. Enum fields go stale exactly when you need them most.

## index.md Drift Policy

`index.md` is a routing table with a scanning-friendly TL;DR column. It is *allowed to drift* from the TL;DR inside each doc — the doc body is authoritative. Update `index.md` when you create or delete a doc, or when the existing TL;DR is so wrong it actively misleads. Don't churn it on every doc edit.

## Core Principles (CODE)

Documentation exists to advance work, not to hoard information. Four steps when handling information:

1. **Capture**: Only record what materially advances the project. When in doubt, leave it out.

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 PegaInfer 全景与 kv-cache 的位置

本讲是学习手册第一讲，为 pegainfer-kv-cache 建立全景：只读仓库架构指南、依赖清单、19 行的 lib.rs 与各类型的文档注释。核心结论：PegaInfer 是纯 Rust+CUDA 推理引擎，各模型线自持调度器与请求状态；共享分页 KV 原语集中在本 crate，host/SSD/RDMA 卸载桥在 pegainfer-kv-offload。核心设计是逻辑/物理两层分离：BlockPool 管块的发放、共享与回收但不持显存，KvBuffer 一次性持有显存但不带分配器，两者靠块 ID 关联。引入词汇表：页几何 KvLayout、全注意力配对门面 KvCacheManager（MLA 模型绕过直用 BlockPool）、每请求 RequestKv 走调度→视图→应用生命周期、内核视图 KvView/KvViewDesc，以及前缀探测、加载预留等池类型和上游 kvbm-logical（本地 fork）的再导出。依赖单向：模型 crate→本 crate→kvbm-logical，故可被多条模型线复用。
### u1-l2 crate 结构、依赖与本地构建测试

本讲从工程侧解剖 pegainfer-kv-cache：五个私有模块正交分工——layout 是纯几何值类型、buffer 持有 bf16 显存但无分配器（指针稳定保障 CUDA Graph 捕获）、pool 为逻辑块池与请求生命周期的绝对核心（约占 src 七成）、manager 把同几何的池与缓冲配成引擎级门面、view 打包内核只读视图；公共 API 共 11 个自有类型，并再导出 kvbm_logical 与 KvCacheEvent 以保证类型同一。Cargo.toml 仅 17 行，7 个依赖全部经 workspace 继承单一版本：cudarc 封装 CUDA 驱动、kvbm-logical 为本地 fork 的块管理器地基、dynamo-kv-hashing 钉 rev 做 LoRA 加盐哈希、half 提供 bf16、tokio 只用 broadcast 事件通道。测试分两层：restore_commit 纯逻辑、无 GPU 也能跑，兼作 #704 注册成本回归锚；lifecycle 需真实 CUDA 设备。约定：命令一律 --release，用 -p 限定作用域。
### u1-l3 分页 KV 与页优先布局 KvLayout

本讲围绕 pegainfer-kv-cache 的三个最小模块展开：layout.rs 的纯值类型 KvLayout、buffer.rs 的物理缓冲 KvBuffer、pool.rs 的逻辑块池 BlockPool，并以 qwen3 消费侧的显存预算代码交叉验证。核心结论：KV 缓存按固定大小、可散布的页管理，既消除外部碎片，又带来前缀块共享、CUDA Graph 指针稳定、整页一次连续拷贝三项引擎级能力；BlockPool 只发放块 ID 不持显存，KvBuffer 一次性分配全部显存且地址永不移动，二者靠页号（块 ID）关联。关键术语是三个步长的纯乘法链，由 num_layers、num_kv_heads（GQA 下缓存只按 KV 头数计）、head_dim、page_size 推出：kv_block_len 是单个 K 或 V 块的元素数，layer_stride 是页内跨一层（K 前 V 后），page_stride 是所有层合成的一整页。排布取页优先：页内按层嵌套、层内 K|V，一页恰为一段连续 page_stride 区间，与池以块为管理粒度对齐。字节换算仅差 ×2（bf16）；页尺寸不是自由参数，须取注意力内核合法值（qwen3 限 16/64）；池预留块 0 作 CUDA Graph 的 padding 槽，实际可用块数为总块数减一。
### u2-l1 BlockPool：逻辑块池与 padding 块

本讲解读 `pegainfer-kv-cache` 的 `BlockPool`（src/pool.rs）：它是上游 kvbm-logical `BlockManager` 之上的薄包装——通用块逻辑（空闲/活跃/LRU 非活跃池、分配注册）在上游，引擎语义（padding 预留、容量口径）在包装层；自身不持有显存，只发放块 ID，物理页由模型侧消费者按 ID 索引。核心结论：构造链路 `build` 先校验至少 2 块，以 Allow 复制策略与 LRU 后端建管理器，再经「allocate → stage(默认哈希满块) → register + std::mem::forget」把块 0 永久预留为 padding 块——CUDA Graph 页表已固化哑页号，该块与引擎同寿、绝不回收，否则图回放会污染真实请求的 KV。容量不变式：available 与 max_request_blocks 均为 total − 1，block_size 是每块 token 数，padding_block_id 以 i32 直填页表；释放的注册块进 LRU 非活跃池，是前缀缓存伏笔。请求拿块/还块的生命周期由下一讲 RequestKv 承接。
### u2-l2 RequestKv：一个请求的 KV 生命周期

2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. - `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

10	/// Engine-level KV cache for full-attention models: one logical
11	/// [`BlockPool`] + one GPU [`KvBuffer`] with matching geometry.
12	///
13	/// MLA models (kimi-k2) consume [`BlockPool`] directly and own their
14	/// physical buffers — this facade is the full-attention pairing only.
15	pub struct KvCacheManager {
16	    pool: BlockPool,
17	    buffer: KvBuffer,
18	}

20	impl KvCacheManager {
21	    pub fn new(
22	        stream: &Arc<CudaStream>,
23	        num_layers: usize,
24	        num_kv_heads: usize,
25	        head_dim: usize,
26	        block_size: usize,
27	        num_blocks: usize,
28	    ) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
29	        Self::new_with_scratch_pages(
30	            stream,
31	            num_layers,
32	            num_kv_heads,
33	            head_dim,
34	            block_size,
35	            num_blocks,
36	            0,
37	        )
38	    }
39	
40	    /// Like [`new`](Self::new), plus `scratch_pages` extra pages in the GPU
41	    /// buffer that the pool never hands out. Their page ids are
42	    /// `num_blocks..num_blocks + scratch_pages`; ownership and content are the
43	    /// caller's business (e.g. the speculative hedge's alternative-chain verify
44	    /// KV). The transaction layer is unaware of them by construction.
45	    pub fn new_with_scratch_pages(
46	        stream: &Arc<CudaStream>,
47	        num_layers: usize,
48	        num_kv_heads: usize,
49	        head_dim: usize,
50	        block_size: usize,
51	        num_blocks: usize,
52	        scratch_pages: usize,
53	    ) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
54	        let buffer = KvBuffer::new(
55	            stream,
56	            num_layers,
57	            num_kv_heads,
58	            head_dim,
59	            block_size,
60	            num_blocks.checked_add(scratch_pages).ok_or_else(|| {
61	                anyhow::anyhow!("KV pages {num_blocks} + scratch {scratch_pages} overflow")
62	            })?,
63	        )?;
64	        let pool = BlockPool::new(block_size, num_blocks)?;
65	        Ok(Self { pool, buffer })
66	    }

69	    ///
70	    /// `num_blocks` may be smaller than the physical allocation. Tensor-parallel
71	    /// executors use this to choose the minimum common logical capacity across
72	    /// rank-local buffers while keeping one shared page-id namespace.
73	    pub fn from_buffer(buffer: KvBuffer, num_blocks: usize) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
74	        anyhow::ensure!(
75	            num_blocks <= buffer.num_blocks(),
76	            "logical KV block count {num_blocks} exceeds physical buffer capacity {}",
77	            buffer.num_blocks()
78	        );

# KV 事件流与缓存感知路由

## 1. 本讲目标
## 2. 前置知识
## 3. 本讲源码地图
## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
### 4.1 事件通道的构造：KV_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY 与 BlockPool::with_events
#### 4.1.1 概念说明
#### 4.1.2 核心流程
#### 4.1.3 源码精读
#### 4.1.4 代码实践
#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案
### 4.2 公共入口 KvCacheManager::new_with_events 与类型再导出
### 4.3 emitted_blocks 光标与 take_newly_registered_blocks / RegisteredBlock
### 4.4 事件消费契约：忽略 Create、封块点自产 store、Remove 反查
## 5. 综合实践
## 6. 本讲小结
## 7. 下一步学习建议

Key facts to weave in:

**背景/动机（承接 u2-l5、u3-l1）**：
- 单机内，前缀缓存在 BlockPool 的非活跃池 + LRU 后端内完成（u2-l5）。
- 多机/路由场景：一个 out-of-band 的「缓存感知路由器」想知道每个 worker 上有哪些前缀块，才能把共享同一前缀的请求调度到同一个 worker（cache-aware routing，即把请求路由到已持有其前缀 KV 的副本，避免重算 prefill）。
- 路由器维护一棵前缀树（radix tree），Create→插入、Remove→摘除。失步 = 树与实际缓存不一致 → 路由决策基于幻觉。

**4.1 通道构造**：
- pool.rs L20-24: KV_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY = 65_536，注释原文："Broadcast capacity for the opt-in KV-event feed. Generous: the scheduler drains it every step, but a step can register/evict many blocks, and a dropped event silently desyncs the router's prefix tree. Only allocated on the BlockPool::with_events path."
- 容量为何宽裕：tokio broadcast 是环形缓冲，慢消费者落后超过容量会收到 Lagged，被跳过的事件永久丢失。一步内可能注册/逐出很多块（大 prompt prefill 一步封几十上百块；evict_inactive 冷冲刷一次逐出整池），64 倍于上游默认 1024。丢一个事件 = 路由前缀树失步（多了一个幽灵条目或少了一个实际存在条目），且无自愈机制——后续事件不会修正历史。
- with_events 是 pub(crate)：crate 内部复用（manager 门面调用），外部使用者走 KvCacheManager::new_with_events。
- 构造流程：EventsManager::builder().channel_capacity(65_536).build() → Arc → events.subscribe_receiver() 拿 rx（subscribe_receiver 而非 subscribe：调用方是非异步调度线程同步 try_recv 排水，必须能观察到 Lagged 而不是被 Stream 过滤掉——上游注释原文）→ BlockRegistry::builder().event_manager(events).build() → 传给 build() 复用通用构造（padding 预留等完全一样）。
- 默认发射策略是 AllEventsPolicy（每个块都跟踪）——pool.rs L54 注释。

**上游机制（背景，简要）**：
- KvCacheEvent = Create(SequenceHash) | Remove(SequenceHash)（protocol.rs L28-34），携带的是 kvbm 128 位 lineage 哈希（SequenceHash），不是路由侧 u64。
- EventsManager.on_block_registered（manager.rs L173-189）：块注册进 BlockRegistry 时发 Create，并给注册句柄挂一个 EventReleaseHandle（RAII）；最后一个引用 drop 时发 Remove（protocol.rs L85-91）。
- 默认容量 1024（EventsManagerSettings L56-57），本 crate 提到 65_536。

**4.2 公共入口**：
- manager.rs L83-103: new_with_events，签名与 new 完全相同，多返回 broadcast::Receiver<KvCacheEvent>。内部先建 KvBuffer（同 new），再 BlockPool::with_events。
- 注意：new_with_events 没有 scratch_pages 参数（不支持投机 scratch 组合——事实上看代码，它直接 KvBuffer::new 不带 scratch）。
- lib.rs L9: `pub use kvbm_logical::events::KvCacheEvent;` 保证类型同一性——外部消费者无需直接依赖 kvbm-logical 也能写出 `pegainfer_kv_cache::KvCacheEvent` 且与通道内流动的是同一类型。
- OFF by default 的原因（pool.rs L47-49 注释原文）："OFF by default: plain single-machine serving uses new and pays neither the per-block event attachment nor the channel." 代价有二：(a) 每个块注册都要挂事件附件（EventReleaseHandle，RAII 附件 + 每次 send）；(b) 通道本身分配。单机服务用不到路由，付这钱纯浪费。
- 现状：工作区内目前没有模型 crate 调用 new_with_events / take_newly_registered_blocks（grep 验证），即这是一条为分布式路由准备、尚未接线的 opt-in 通道。（我在 grep 全仓库时只命中了 transcript 文件。要小心表述——写「截至当前 HEAD，workspace 内尚无模型 crate 消费这两个入口（grep 验证）」。）

**4.3 emitted_blocks 光标与 take_newly_registered_blocks / RegisteredBlock**：
- RequestKv 结构体（L373-388）：seq + emitted_blocks: usize。doc 原文："Cursor for take_newly_registered_blocks: how many of this request's sequence blocks have already been surfaced as KV-router store events. Starts past the prefix-cache hit (those were stored by whoever first sealed them — this assumes GPU-resident reuse, i.e. KV offload off, which holds wherever the event feed is enabled). Untouched on the plain path where the feed is off."
- 两个初始化点：new_request_with_cache_salt 时 0（L185）；match_and_add_prefix_up_to 后设为 assigned_blocks()（L421）——跳过前缀命中块，理由（L418-421 注释）："Prefix-hit blocks are already in the router's tree (whoever first sealed them stored them, and a GPU hit means they were never evicted), so the store-event cursor skips them."
- 隐含假设：事件流开启的地方 KV offload 必须是关的。若开启，恢复块可能从未在本机发过 Create/对应 store 事件，光标语义就破了。这是显式记录的设计耦合。
- take_newly_registered_blocks（L696-718）算法：
  - registered = seq.assigned_blocks()（已注册=已拿到 ImmutableBlock=可被他人复用）
  - 若 registered <= emitted_blocks 返回空 vec
  - debug_assert registered <= blocks.len()（注册数不超过已封 token 块数）
  - 切片 blocks[emitted_blocks..registered]，每个映射成 RegisteredBlock { plh: kvbm_sequence_hash().as_u128(), sequence_hash: b.sequence_hash(), tokens_hash: b.block_hash(), parent_sequence_hash: b.parent_sequence_hash() }
  - 光标推进到 registered
- 注册滞后封块一步的细节（L691-694 注释）："A block becomes reusable by other requests once it is registered (assigned an ImmutableBlock), which lags sealing the token block by a step."——因此以 assigned_blocks 而非 sealed blocks 为准。
- RegisteredBlock（L721-733）两套哈希体系：
  - plh: u128 —— 引擎 128 位 lineage 哈希（kvbm SequenceHash），仅用于把逐出事件（携带 lineage 哈希）关联回 sequence_hash。
  - sequence_hash/tokens_hash/parent_sequence_hash: u64 —— 路由侧哈希（dynamo_tokens::TokenBlock 访问器，与路由器重算的逐位相同——by construction）。
  - 父哈希 Option：首块没有父。
  - 两套体系并存的原因：路由器（dynamo 生态）用 u64 哈希族建前缀树；引擎内部（kvbm）用 128 位 lineage 哈希标识块身份；逐出事件只携带 lineage，所以消费者必须存 plh→sequence_hash 映射来反查。

**4.4 事件消费契约**：
- pool.rs L44-48 注释原文："The stream carries Create events too (the emission policy can't separate them) — the consumer ignores Create and sources richer store events from the seal site, and maps the lineage hash in each Remove back to the router's sequence_hash."
- 为何忽略 Create：AllEventsPolicy 无法把 Create 单独关掉，通道里必然混着 Create。但 Create 只带一个 SequenceHash，信息太穷（没有路由侧 u64 哈希、没有父链接）；而封块点（seal site）调用方自己能通过 take_newly_registered_blocks 拿到全量 RegisteredBlock，含四元组。所以 store 事件在封块点自产更丰富。
- Remove 反查：Remove(SequenceHash) 只有 lineage 哈希 → 消费者维护 plh→sequence_hash 表（从自产 store 事件积累），Remove 到来时查表得到路由树要摘除的节点键。
- 消费节奏：调度器每步排水（drains it every step——常量注释原文），用 try_recv 同步抽干直到 RecvError::Empty / Lagged。Lagged = 有事件被丢 = 前缀树已失步（风险模型：这不是可恢复错误，路由树从此带幻觉；容量 64K 就是为了让这种情况在实际速率下不可能发生）。
- 为何 pub(crate) with_events + pub new_with_events 的分层：把「带事件的池」这个实现细节留在 crate 内，公共 API 只暴露门面，保证 BlockPool 的构造表面不扩大（呼应 #858 公共面收缩——这个里程碑在 u3-l3 讲，我提一句即可，不展开，且我不确定 #858 具体内容与 with_events 相关，谨慎表述为「公共面保持窄」）。

小心：不要断言 #858 与事件 API 的关系。我在 u3-l3 大纲里看到「公共面收缩(#858)」。我可以说「与 crate 一贯的窄公共面风格一致」，不点名提交。

**风险模型小结**（学习目标 1）：

The `commit_extends_partial_gpu_hit` test shows a fully pure-logical path that registers blocks: `new_request` → `schedule_prefill` → `apply_prefill` → blocks get registered. No GPU needed. So a reader can write a pure-logic test exercising `take_newly_registered_blocks`:

```rust
let mut seed = pool.new_request(prompt, 1, None);
seed.schedule_prefill(3 * BLOCK_SIZE, &pool).unwrap();
seed.apply_prefill(1, &pool).unwrap();
let new_blocks = seed.take_newly_registered_blocks();
assert_eq!(new_blocks.len(), 3);
// second call returns empty
assert!(seed.take_newly_registered_blocks().is_empty());
// a second request matching the prefix emits nothing for the matched blocks
let mut req2 = pool.new_request(same_prompt_longer, 4, None);
req2.match_and_add_prefix(&pool).unwrap();
assert!(req2.take_newly_registered_blocks().is_empty()); // cursor starts past the hit
```

Wait — for the second request after match_and_add_prefix, emitted_blocks = assigned_blocks() = 3 (matched blocks are assigned). take_newly_registered_blocks → registered = 3 <= emitted = 3 → empty. Yes! That validates the "skip prefix hit" semantics. This is a great practice test.

Also can validate RegisteredBlock fields: plh is u128, parent_sequence_hash None for first block, Some for second, and that sequence_hash of block i+1 == parent chain... Actually `parent_sequence_hash` of block i should equal `sequence_hash` of block i-1? In dynamo tokens, sequence_hash is chained: block i's sequence_hash derives from parent's sequence_hash + block hash. It's plausible that `blocks[i].parent_sequence_hash() == Some(blocks[i-1].sequence_hash())`. I shouldn't assert this without verification — I can suggest observing it as an experiment ("观察 plh 与 sequence_hash 的关系、验证相邻块的 parent 链接", marked 待本地验证 if uncertain). Safer: assert first block's parent_sequence_hash is None, subsequent are Some. That's implied by Option semantics but even that — for the first block there is no parent so None. # KV 事件流与缓存感知路由

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清 `KV_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY = 65_536` 这个「宽裕」容量背后的风险模型：为什么丢一个事件就等于让路由器的前缀树永久失步，以及这个模型如何反过来决定了容量、排水节奏与「默认关闭」三件事。
2. 复述事件通道的完整构造链：`KvCacheManager::new_with_events`（唯一公共入口）→ `BlockPool::with_events`（`pub(crate)` 内部实现）→ 上游 `kvbm-logical` 的 `EventsManager` / `BlockRegistry` / `tokio::broadcast`。
3. 梳理 `RegisteredBlock` 里并存的**两套哈希体系**：引擎侧 128 位 lineage 哈希（`plh`）与路由侧 u64 哈希（`sequence_hash` / `tokens_hash` / `parent_sequence_hash`），以及为什么逐出事件需要从前者反查后者。
4. 独立推导一个事件消费者的实现契约：忽略 `Create`、在封块点用 `take_newly_registered_blocks` 自产更丰富的 store 事件、把 `Remove` 映射回路由树的节点键。

本讲是专家层的第二讲，承接 u2-l5（前缀缓存与 lineage 哈希链）与 u3-l1（恢复-提交链路）。前面两讲解决的是「单机内缓存如何命中与恢复」，本讲回答的是：**当缓存分布在多个 worker 上时，谁来告诉调度器哪个 worker 手里有哪段前缀？**

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 缓存感知路由（cache-aware router）

多副本部署里，同一个 prompt 前缀（比如相同的系统提示词）可能已经在 worker A 上算过 prefill。如果新请求被路由到 A，就能直接跳过这段 prefill；路由到 B 就得重算。**缓存感知路由器**就是干这件事的组件：它给每个 worker 维护一棵**前缀树**（radix tree）——「这个 worker 手里有哪些前缀块」，然后按请求的 token 前缀选目标 worker。

路由器是 **out-of-band**（带外）的：它不在请求的转发路径上做计算，只是旁路订阅每个引擎的 KV 块事件流，据此更新自己那棵树。本讲的主角就是这条旁路事件流。

### 2.2 tokio broadcast 的三条语义

`tokio::sync::broadcast` 是多生产者多消费者通道，理解本讲必须先知道它的三条行为：

1. **环形缓冲 + 定容**：通道容量在创建时固定。容量之内的事件不会阻塞发送方——发送方只管往里塞。
2. **Lagged = 丢历史**：某个接收者消费太慢、落后超过容量时，它会收到一个 `Lagged` 错误，**被跳过的事件永久丢失**，之后继续收新事件。没有补发机制。
3. **晚订阅丢更早的事件**：订阅只从订阅时刻开始收；之前发生的事件看不见。

本讲所有的设计决策——容量 65_536、每步排水、构造前先订阅——都是对这三条语义的回应。

### 2.3 RAII 与 Drop 钩子

Rust 的 RAII 惯用法：把「释放时的副作用」写进一个句柄类型的 `Drop` 实现里。上游 kvbm-logical 用它实现 Remove 事件——块注册时挂一个 `EventReleaseHandle`，当块的最后一个引用被丢弃（被逐出/释放）时，`Drop` 自动广播 `Remove`。你在 u2-l1 已经见过同款手法（`ImmutableBlock` 的 RAII 保证 padding 块不回空闲池）。

### 2.4 回顾：lineage 哈希链

u2-l5 讲过：每个缓存块的身份 = 位置 + 块内容 + 父块哈希 + salt 构成的 **lineage 哈希链**（kvbm 的 128 位 `SequenceHash`）。共享前缀逐位相同、分叉即全变。本讲会看到同一个 128 位哈希在两套消费体系里的两种用途。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 角色 |
|------|------|
| `src/pool.rs` | 绝对主角：容量常量 `KV_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY`、`BlockPool::with_events`、`RequestKv::emitted_blocks` 光标、`take_newly_registered_blocks`、`RegisteredBlock` |
| `src/manager.rs` | 唯一公共入口 `KvCacheManager::new_with_events` |
| `src/lib.rs` | `KvCacheEvent` 从 kvbm-logical 的再导出，保证类型同一性 |
| `kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/protocol.rs`（上游依赖） | `KvCacheEvent` 枚举定义、`EventReleaseHandle` 的 Drop→Remove 机制 |
| `kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs`（上游依赖） | `EventsManager`：发射策略、通道容量默认值、`subscribe_receiver`、`on_block_registered` 钩子 |

注意后两个文件在 `pegainfer-kv-cache` 之外——它们是本 crate 的上游依赖 `kvbm-logical`（workspace 内的本地 fork，见根 `Cargo.toml` 的 `kvbm/kvbm-logical` path 依赖）。本讲引用它们是为了把「事件从哪来」讲透；日常开发中你只需要消费本 crate 的公共 API。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 通道的构造：`KV_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY` 与 `BlockPool::with_events`

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

普通 `BlockPool::new` 构造的池是「哑」的：块注册、逐出都只发生在池内部，外界无从得知。`with_events` 构造的池则额外挂了一条事件流：每当有块注册（可被他人复用）或块被彻底丢弃（逐出），都会向通道广播一个事件。路由器订阅这条流，就能把「每个 worker 有哪些前缀块」实时镜像成一棵前缀树。

这里有一个先讲直觉的风险模型，它解释了后面所有数字：

> 路由器的前缀树是**纯增量镜像**——`Create`/store 插入、`Remove` 摘除。没有任何对账协议可以让树重新和实际缓存对齐。所以**丢一个事件，树就和现实永久不一致**：树里多出一个幽灵块（路由器会把请求派去一个其实没有该前缀的 worker），或少一个实际存在的块（前缀复用机会被浪费）。两种都不崩，但都让路由决策建立在幻觉上。

既然「丢事件 = 不可恢复的失步」，设计就只剩两道防线：**容量足够宽裕** + **消费足够勤快**。容量常量的注释把这两点都写明了。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`with_events` 的构造流程：

```text
BlockPool::with_events(block_size, num_blocks)
  1. EventsManager::builder()
       .channel_capacity(65_536)        ← 覆盖上游默认 1024
       .build()                          ← 默认 AllEventsPolicy：每块都跟踪
  2. events.subscribe_receiver()         ← 在建池【之前】订阅 → 一个事件不漏
  3. BlockRegistry::builder()
       .event_manager(events).build()    ← 注册表挂上事件钩子
  4. Self::build(block_size, num_blocks, registry)
       ↑ 与普通 new 完全共用同一条构造路径（含 padding 块预留）
```

普通 `new` 与 `with_events` 的**唯一**区别是第 3 步传进 `build` 的注册表：`new` 传一个不带事件管理器的裸 `BlockRegistry`（[src/pool.rs:L38-L40](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L38-L40)），`with_events` 传挂了钩子的。块的分配、封块、前缀匹配、LRU 逐出逻辑一个字都不用改——事件是纯旁路观测。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看容量常量及其注释——这是本讲最重要的一段注释：

> ```rust
> /// Broadcast capacity for the opt-in KV-event feed. Generous: the scheduler
> /// drains it every step, but a step can register/evict many blocks, and a
> /// dropped event silently desyncs the router's prefix tree. Only allocated on
> /// the [`BlockPool::with_events`] path.
> const KV_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY: usize = 65_536;
> ```

- [src/pool.rs:L20-L24](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L20-L24)：容量 65_536。注释三句话对应三个事实：**宽裕**（Generous）——一步可能注册/逐出很多块；**失步是静默的**（silently desyncs）——没有报错、没有自愈；**只有 with_events 路径才付这个分配**（Only allocated on … path）。

再对比上游默认值，体会「宽裕」是相对谁说的：

- [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs:L44-L58](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs#L44-L58)：`EventsManagerSettings` 的 `channel_capacity` 默认 `1024`。本 crate 显式提到 65_536，是默认值的 **64 倍**。

为什么必须放大？做个数量级估算（示例演算，不是源码断言）：block_size = 16 时，一个 8192 token 的 prompt 一步 prefill 就要注册 \(\lceil 8192/16 \rceil = 512\) 个块；`evict_inactive` 冷冲刷（u2-l5 讲过）一次性逐出整个非活跃池——一个 4096 块的池就是上千个 Remove。若消费者一步之内没来得及排空而突发量超过容量，`Lagged` 就触发。安全条件可以写成：

\[
E_{\text{step}} \;=\; \#\text{新注册块} + \#\text{逐出块} \;\le\; C = 65\,536
\]

65_536 给单步突发留了数十倍余量，让这个条件在实际速率下不可能被打破。

接着看 `with_events` 本体：

- [src/pool.rs:L50-L64](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L50-L64)：

  ```rust
  pub(crate) fn with_events(
      block_size: usize,
      num_blocks: usize,
  ) -> anyhow::Result<(Self, broadcast::Receiver<KvCacheEvent>)> {
      // Default emission policy is AllEventsPolicy (every block tracked).
      let events = Arc::new(
          EventsManager::builder()
              .channel_capacity(KV_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY)
              .build(),
      );
      let rx = events.subscribe_receiver();
      let registry = BlockRegistry::builder().event_manager(events).build();
      let pool = Self::build(block_size, num_blocks, registry)?;
      Ok((pool, rx))
  }
  ```

  三个细节值得停下来：

  1. **`pub(crate)` 可见性**——它不是公共 API，外部使用者不能直接调（4.2 讲公共入口）。把「带事件的池」留在 crate 内部，`BlockPool` 对外的构造面就保持最窄。
  2. **`subscribe_receiver()` 而非 `subscribe()`**——上游对这两个方法的取舍有明确注释：[kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs:L153-L159](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs#L153-L159)：「给需要**同步排水**的调用方（比如从非异步的调度线程 `try_recv`），且**必须观察到 `Lagged`** 而不是让它被悄悄过滤掉」。`subscribe()` 返回的 Stream 会把 `Lagged` 错误直接滤掉——对本讲的风险模型来说那是灾难性的静默；裸 Receiver 才能让消费者看见失步。
  3. **先订阅、后建池**——`rx` 在 `Self::build` 之前拿到手，所以从块 0（padding 块）注册起的全部事件都可见，不存在晚订阅丢事件的问题。

最后看事件本身长什么样（上游定义）：

- [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/protocol.rs:L28-L34](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/protocol.rs#L28-L34)：

  ```rust
  pub enum KvCacheEvent {
      /// A block has been registered in a worker's cache.
      Create(SequenceHash),
      /// A block has been removed from a worker's cache.
      Remove(SequenceHash),
  }
  ```

  两个变体**都只携带一个 `SequenceHash`**——kvbm 的 128 位 lineage 哈希。注意这个信息量：`Create` 既没有路由侧哈希，也没有父块链接。这个「穷」直接导致了 4.4 的消费契约。

- [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/protocol.rs:L64-L91](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/protocol.rs#L64-L91)：`EventReleaseHandle` 持有 `(seq_hash, event_tx)`，其 `Drop` 实现 `send(Remove(seq_hash))`。它作为附件挂在块的注册句柄上（挂接动作在 [events/manager.rs:L173-L189](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs#L173-L189) 的 `on_block_registered` 里完成）：块注册时发 `Create` + 挂附件，块最后一个引用消失时附件 `Drop` 发 `Remove`。发送失败（无接收者）被显式忽略——`let _ = send(...)`。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `with_events` 用 `subscribe_receiver()` 拿裸 Receiver，而不用返回 Stream 的 `subscribe()`？

**参考答案**：消费方是引擎调度线程，需要用 `try_recv` 同步排水，不能依赖 async 运行时；更关键的是，`subscribe()` 返回的 Stream 会把 `Lagged` 错误悄悄过滤掉（上游注释原文："The stream filters out lagged errors … and continues delivering subsequent events"），而本讲的风险模型要求消费者**必须**能观察到 `Lagged`——它是「前缀树已失步」的唯一信号。裸 `broadcast::Receiver` 的 `try_recv` 会把 `Lagged` 作为错误返回。

**练习 2**：如果把 `KV_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY` 改回上游默认的 1024，最可能先出问题的场景是哪个：长 prompt 的一次性 prefill、多个并发请求的常规 decode、还是 `evict_inactive` 冷冲刷？

**参考答案**：`evict_inactive` 冷冲刷。常规 decode 每步每请求至多注册一两个块，量级很小；长 prompt prefill 一步注册 \(\lceil L/b \rceil\) 块，16k token / block_size 16 也只有 1024 块，刚好贴着容量；而冷冲刷一次逐出**整个非活跃池**，池有数千块时会瞬间产生数千个 Remove，轻松越过 1024，消费者一步没排水就 `Lagged` 失步。

**练习 3**：接收者是在建池之前订阅的。据此推断：消费者收到的**第一个**事件可能是什么？（提示：回忆 u2-l1 的 padding 块构造。）

**参考答案**：padding 块的 `Create` 事件。`build` 路径会 `register_block` 注册块 0（u2-l1 讲过：stage 默认哈希 → 注册 → `std::mem::forget`），注册走挂了钩子的 `BlockRegistry`，于是广播 `Create(SequenceHash::default())`。又因为 padding 块被 `std::mem::forget` 永久遗忘、其注册句柄永不 Drop，这个块**永远不会有对应的 Remove**。消费者应当预期这个「开场事件」并将其忽略。（此推断基于注册钩子的挂接机制，具体是否命中待本地验证。）

### 4.2 公共入口：`KvCacheManager::new_with_events` 与类型再导出

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

4.1 的 `BlockPool::with_events` 是 `pub(crate)`——外部使用者拿不到。真正暴露给模型 crate / 服务进程的入口在门面 `KvCacheManager` 上。这个分层有两层含义：

1. **门面职责**（u1-l1 讲过）：`KvCacheManager` 把逻辑池和同几何的物理 `KvBuffer` 配成一对，是全注意力模型的引擎级入口。事件能力作为「构造期选项」挂在门面上，而不是散落成裸池的公共构造器，公共面保持窄。
2. **类型同一性**：事件通道里流动的 `KvCacheEvent` 定义在上游 kvbm-logical。如果每个消费者都自己去依赖 kvbm-logical，版本或路径一旦分叉，通道两端的类型就不是同一个，`Receiver<KvCacheEvent>` 对不上。`lib.rs` 的再导出把这个问题钉死。

还有一个显式的设计立场：**默认关闭**。注释原文写明了成本项——单机服务不为路由器付一分钱。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
KvCacheManager::new_with_events(stream, 几何参数..., num_blocks)
  → KvBuffer::new(...)                    ← 物理缓冲，与 new 完全一样
  → BlockPool::with_events(block_size, num_blocks)
       → (pool, rx)
  → Ok((KvCacheManager { pool, buffer }, rx))   ← 元组：门面 + 事件接收器
```

调用方拿到 `(manager, rx)` 后：`manager` 照常走 `pool()` / `buffer()` 做推理；`rx` 交给旁路的路由器组件排水。两条路径互不干扰——这正是「带外」的含义。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

- [src/manager.rs:L83-L103](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/manager.rs#L83-L103)：

  ```rust

  /// receiver to drain. See [`BlockPool::with_events`].

      stream: &Arc<CudaStream>,
      num_layers: usize,
      num_kv_heads: usize,
      head_dim: usize,
      block_size: usize,
      num_blocks: usize,
  ) -> anyhow::Result<(Self, broadcast::Receiver<KvCacheEvent>)> {
      let buffer = KvBuffer::new(...)?;
      let (pool, events) = BlockPool::with_events(block_size, num_blocks)?;
      Ok((Self { pool, buffer }, events))
  }
  ```

  三个观察点：

### 4.3 封块点自产事件：`emitted_blocks` 光标、`take_newly_registered_blocks` 与 `RegisteredBlock`

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

4.1 说过通道里的 `Create(SequenceHash)` 信息很穷：只有一个 128 位 lineage 哈希，没有路由侧需要的 u64 哈希族，也没有父块链接。那路由器的 store（插入）事件从哪来？答案：**调用方在封块点自己造**。

`RequestKv` 上有一条与请求生命周期平行的「事件产出」机制：一个 `emitted_blocks` 光标记录「这个请求的序列块里，已经有多少个被作为 store 事件汇报给路由器了」，`take_newly_registered_blocks()` 则每次返回自上次调用以来**新注册**的块，打包成信息完整的 `RegisteredBlock` 四元组。调度循环里每个 apply 之后调一次，就能把本请求新贡献给缓存的块如实上报。

而 `RegisteredBlock` 里并存两套哈希体系，是本讲最值得咀嚼的设计：

| 字段 | 位宽 | 体系 | 用途 |
|------|------|------|------|
| `plh` | u128 | 引擎侧（kvbm lineage 哈希） | 与逐出事件对账：`Remove` 只携带 lineage 哈希，靠它反查 |
| `sequence_hash` | u64 | 路由侧（dynamo_tokens） | 路由前缀树的节点键 |
| `tokens_hash` | u64 | 路由侧 | 块内容哈希 |
| `parent_sequence_hash` | `Option<u64>` | 路由侧 | 父块链接，串成链；首块为 `None` |

两套体系各服务一个消费者：引擎内部（前缀匹配、LRU、offload 寻址）用 128 位 lineage；dynamo 生态的路由器用 u64 哈希族建树。`RegisteredBlock` 同时携带两者，等于在块注册的一瞬间完成了一次「双语登记」。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

`emitted_blocks` 光标的推进规则（配合 u2-l2 的三拍生命周期阅读）：

```text
new_request(...)                     emitted_blocks = 0
    │
match_and_add_prefix / _up_to        emitted_blocks = assigned_blocks()
    │                                （跳过前缀命中块：它们已由首次封块者上报过）
    │
schedule → forward → apply …         每次应用后新块可能被注册
    │
take_newly_registered_blocks()       registered = assigned_blocks()
    │                                若 registered <= emitted_blocks → 返回空
    │                                否则返回 blocks[emitted_blocks..registered]
    │                                并把光标推到 registered
    ▼
（下一拍继续增量产出）
```

`take_newly_registered_blocks` 的算法骨架：

```text
输入: self（请求）, 光标 emitted_blocks
1. registered ← seq.assigned_blocks()          // 已拿到 ImmutableBlock 的块数
2. 若 registered ≤ emitted_blocks: 返回 []       // 本拍没有新注册
3. blocks ← seq.inner().sequence().blocks()     // 按序排列的 token 块
4. debug_assert!(registered ≤ blocks.len())     // 注册数不超过已封 token 块数
5. 对 blocks[emitted_blocks..registered] 逐块映射:
       plh                 ← b.kvbm_sequence_hash().as_u128()
       sequence_hash       ← b.sequence_hash()
       tokens_hash         ← b.block_hash()
       parent_sequence_hash← b.parent_sequence_hash()
6. emitted_blocks ← registered; 返回新块列表（序列序）
```

以 `assigned_blocks`（已注册）而非「已封 token 块」为准是有讲究的——源码注释说明：「A block becomes reusable by other requests once it is *registered* (assigned an `ImmutableBlock`), which lags sealing the token block by a step.」可复用性与注册绑定，路由器只该看见已可复用的块。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

- [src/pool.rs:L379-L388](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L379-L388)：`RequestKv` 结构体与光标字段的完整文档：

  ```rust
  pub struct RequestKv {
      seq: SchedulableSequence<()>,
      /// Cursor for [`Self::take_newly_registered_blocks`]: how many of this
      /// request's sequence blocks have already been surfaced as KV-router store
      /// events. Starts past the prefix-cache hit (those were stored by whoever
      /// first sealed them — this assumes GPU-resident reuse, i.e. KV offload off,
      /// which holds wherever the event feed is enabled). Untouched on the plain
  ```

  这段注释里藏着一个**显式声明的设计耦合**：光标跳过前缀命中块的前提是「这些块从未离开过 GPU」——即 **KV offload 关闭**。注释接着说这个前提「holds wherever the event feed is enabled」（事件流开启的地方该前提都成立）：事件流与 offload 目前是互斥使用的两个 opt-in 世界。若两者同开，从 CPU 层恢复的块可能从未在本机发过 store 事件，光标语义就破了。

- [src/pool.rs:L183-L186](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L183-L186)：构造时光标清零——`RequestKv { seq, emitted_blocks: 0 }`。

- [src/pool.rs:L414-L422](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L414-L422)：`match_and_add_prefix_up_to` 尾部，光标的第二个初始化点：

  ```rust
  let blocks = self.seq.match_and_add_prefix_up_to(&pool.block_manager, max_blocks)?;
  // Prefix-hit blocks are already in the router's tree (whoever first sealed
  // them stored them, and a GPU hit means they were never evicted),
  // so the store-event cursor skips them.
  self.emitted_blocks = self.seq.assigned_blocks();
  ```

  命中块直接计入「已上报」——它们的上报责任属于第一次封存它们的那个请求（u2-l5 的非活跃池复活机制保证 GPU 命中块从未被逐出，所以那次上报仍然有效）。

- [src/pool.rs:L688-L718](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L688-L718)：`take_newly_registered_blocks` 全文（方法文档 + 实现，伪代码已在上文展开）。注意它是 `&mut self`——推进光标是内部状态变更；返回 `Vec<RegisteredBlock>`，本拍无新块时为空。

- [src/pool.rs:L721-L733](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L721-L733)：`RegisteredBlock` 及其文档，两套哈希的分工写得非常直白：

  ```rust
  /// One full KV block a request just registered, ready to become a KV-router
  /// store event. `sequence_hash`/`tokens_hash`/`parent_sequence_hash` are the
  /// router's u64 hashes (`dynamo_tokens::TokenBlock` accessors, identical by
  /// construction to what the router recomputes); `plh` is the engine's 128-bit
  /// lineage hash, kept only to correlate an eviction event (which carries the
  /// lineage hash) back to `sequence_hash`.
  #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
  pub struct RegisteredBlock {
      pub plh: u128,
      pub sequence_hash: u64,
      pub tokens_hash: u64,
      pub parent_sequence_hash: Option<u64>,
  }
  ```

  「identical by construction to what the router recomputes」——路由侧三个哈希取自 `dynamo_tokens::TokenBlock` 的访问器，与路由器自己重算的逐位相同，无需任何翻译。唯一需要翻译的是逐出事件（见 4.4）。

- 对照一个边界：u3-l1 讲过 [src/pool.rs:L735-L739](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L735-L739) 的 `sequence_hash_bytes` 把同一个 128 位 lineage 哈希大端编码成 16 字节**内容键**，那是给 **offload 层**寻址用的；本讲的 `plh` 是同一个哈希在**事件空间**里的形态。一个哈希、两个消费方向、两种编码约定——都收敛在 pool.rs 这一个文件里。

   ```rust
   // 示例代码：读者实践，仿 restore_commit.rs 风格
   use pegainfer_kv_cache::BlockPool;

   const BLOCK_SIZE: usize = 16;

   #[test]
   fn cursor_emits_only_newly_registered_blocks() {
       let pool = BlockPool::new(BLOCK_SIZE, 64).expect("pool");
       // 48 tokens = 3 full blocks；末 token 由 apply 产出
       let prompt: Vec<u32> = (0..48).map(|i| i % 97).collect();

       let mut seed = pool.new_request(prompt.clone(), 1, None);
       // 尚未 apply：没有任何已注册块
       assert!(seed.take_newly_registered_blocks().is_empty());
       seed.schedule_prefill(3 * BLOCK_SIZE, &pool).expect("sched");
       seed.apply_prefill(1, &pool).expect("apply");

       let first = seed.take_newly_registered_blocks();
       assert_eq!(first.len(), 3, "3 full blocks registered at apply");
       assert_eq!(first[0].parent_sequence_hash, None, "genesis block");
       assert!(first[1].parent_sequence_hash.is_some(), "chained");
       // 光标已推进：同拍再取为空
       assert!(seed.take_newly_registered_blocks().is_empty());
       seed.release().expect("release");

       // 同前缀的第二个请求：命中块不再上报（它们由 seed 上报过）
       let mut longer = prompt;
       longer.extend(48..64); // 第 4 块内容不同
       let mut req2 = pool.new_request(longer, 4, None);
       let matched = req2.match_and_add_prefix(&pool).expect("match");
       assert_eq!(matched, 3 * BLOCK_SIZE);
       assert!(req2.take_newly_registered_blocks().is_empty(),
               "prefix-hit blocks are already in the router's tree");
   }
   ```

2. 运行：`cargo test --release -p pegainfer-kv-cache --test events_cursor -- --nocapture`。

**需要观察的现象**：三次断言分别验证光标的三个行为——apply 前为空、apply 后产出 3 块且再次调用为空、命中前缀的后续请求产出为空。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `take_newly_registered_blocks` 以 `assigned_blocks()` 为准，而不是「已封 token 块数」？

**参考答案**：源码注释：「A block becomes reusable by other requests once it is *registered* (assigned an `ImmutableBlock`), which lags sealing the token block by a step.」路由器关心的是「这个块现在能被别的请求复用吗」，只有注册（拿到 `ImmutableBlock`）之后答案才是肯定的。若按已封块上报，路由器可能把尚不可复用的块插进前缀树，把请求派过来却发现匹配失败。

**练习 2**：`emitted_blocks` 光标跳过前缀命中块的前提是什么？如果前提被打破会发生什么？

**参考答案**：前提是「GPU 命中块从未被逐出、其 store 事件已由首次封存者上报且仍然有效」——即 KV offload 关闭（注释原文：「this assumes GPU-resident reuse, i.e. KV offload off, which holds wherever the event feed is enabled」）。若同开 offload：块可能被逐出到 CPU 层、其 store 事件的树节点已被 Remove 摘除，之后从 CPU 恢复回 GPU 再被新请求命中时，光标直接跳过、无人重新上报——路由树里永久缺失这段前缀。这就是两个 opt-in 世界目前互斥的原因。

**练习 3**：`RegisteredBlock::plh` 为什么只在 4.4 要讲的「Remove 反查」里用到，路由树本身不用它做键？

**参考答案**：路由树（dynamo 生态）的插入/查询全部使用 u64 哈希族，与路由器自行重算的值 by construction 一致；而逐出事件来自引擎侧的 kvbm 机制，只携带 128 位 lineage 哈希。`plh` 的唯一职责就是充当两套体系间的**关联键**（注释原文：「kept only to correlate an eviction event (which carries the lineage hash) back to `sequence_hash`」）——消费者存一张 plh→sequence_hash 的表，Remove 到来时查表换算。

### 4.4 事件消费契约与「丢事件即失步」风险模型

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

把 4.1–4.3 拼起来，一个缓存感知路由的消费者必须遵守一套相当反直觉的契约。`with_events` 的文档注释用一句话预告了全部三条：

> ```rust
> /// The stream carries `Create` events too
> /// (the emission policy can't separate them) — the consumer ignores `Create`
> /// and sources richer store events from the seal site, and maps the lineage
> /// hash in each `Remove` back to the router's `sequence_hash`.
> ```

1. **忽略 `Create`**：通道里必然混着 Create（默认 AllEventsPolicy 无法单独关掉 Create），但它的信息量太穷——只有一个 lineage 哈希，没有路由需要的 u64 键和父链接。
2. **store 事件在封块点自产**：即 4.3 的 `take_newly_registered_blocks`——调用方在每个 apply 之后取增量，转成信息完整的 store 事件喂给路由器。
3. **`Remove` 反查**：Remove 携带 lineage 哈希，消费者必须经 `plh → sequence_hash` 映射表换算出路由树要摘除的节点键。

为什么不一改了之——让 `KvCacheEvent` 直接携带更丰富的信息？因为那是上游 kvbm-logical 的公共协议（还要 Serialize 跨 worker 上线，见 [protocol.rs:L28-L34](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/protocol.rs#L28-L34) 的 serde 派生）。本 crate 选择在消费端补齐语义，不动上游协议——这是一个典型的「适配在边界」取舍。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

一个调度循环内嵌事件消费者的伪代码（示例代码，展示契约而非真实实现——截至当前 HEAD，workspace 内尚无此消费者）：

```text
每个引擎步 (step):
  ── 推理路径（主线） ─────────────────────────────
  schedule → view → forward → apply
  for rb in request.take_newly_registered_blocks():   # 封块点自产 store
      router_tree.insert(rb.sequence_hash, rb.tokens_hash, rb.parent_sequence_hash)
      plh_map[rb.plh] = rb.sequence_hash              # 登记反查表

  ── 旁路排水（路由器侧，同一线程或专职线程） ───────
  loop:
      match rx.try_recv():
          Ok(Create(_))        → 忽略（信息穷，见契约 1）
          Ok(Remove(lineage))  → plh_map 查 sequence_hash → router_tree.remove(...)
          Err(Empty)           → break               # 本步排空
          Err(Lagged(n))       → 前缀树已失步！
                                 # n 个事件被丢，无补发协议；
                                 # 只能重建整棵树（或告警 + 降级为非感知路由）
```

风险模型的形式化总结：

- 事件量与消费速率满足 \( E_{\text{step}} \le C \) 时树保持同步；越界即 `Lagged`。
- `Lagged` 之后**没有对账协议**——后续事件不会修正被跳过的历史，失步是永久的。
- 因此防线全在事前：容量宽裕（\( C = 65\,536 \)，上游默认的 64 倍）+ 每步排水（调度器天然提供节拍）+ 默认关闭（没有路由器的部署根本不暴露在这个风险面里）。

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

- 契约的权威出处是 [src/pool.rs:L42-L49](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L42-L49) 的整段文档注释（上文已引）。「the emission policy can't separate them」指上游的 `EventEmissionPolicy` 只能整体开关（[events/manager.rs:L177-L179](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs#L177-L179)：`if !self.policy.should_emit(seq_hash) { return Ok(()); }`——策略只决定「这个块发不发事件」，不区分 Create/Remove），所以 Create 一定会流进来，只能由消费者忽略。

- Remove 的产生机制再确认一遍（它决定了 Remove 的时序语义）：

  - [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs:L173-L189](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs#L173-L189)：注册时 `on_block_registered` 发 `Create` 并把 `EventReleaseHandle` 挂到注册句柄。
  - [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/protocol.rs:L85-L91](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/protocol.rs#L85-L91)：

    ```rust
    impl Drop for EventReleaseHandle {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let event = KvCacheEvent::Remove(self.seq_hash);
            // Broadcast send only fails if there are no receivers, which is fine
            let _ = self.event_tx.send(event);
        }
    }
    ```

    块的最后一个引用消失（活跃请求全部释放且被 LRU 逐出、或 `evict_inactive` 显式冲刷）时，附件 Drop → Remove 入通道。发送失败（无接收者）被显式忽略——这也解释了为什么 Receiver 必须活得和引擎一样久：中途 drop 再重建接收器，期间的 Remove 全部蒸发。

- 排水接口的选择在 [kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs:L153-L159](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/kvbm/kvbm-logical/src/events/manager.rs#L153-L159)：`subscribe_receiver` 的文档明说服务「drain synchronously (e.g. `try_recv` from a non-async scheduler thread)」且「must observe `Lagged` rather than have it silently filtered」——与 4.1.5 练习 1 呼应。

- 「默认关闭」的成本论证出处：[src/pool.rs:L47-L49](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L47-L49)（「pays neither the per-block event attachment nor the channel」）。普通 `new` 的裸注册表构造在 [src/pool.rs:L38-L40](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-kv-cache/src/pool.rs#L38-L40)。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：消费者为什么必须忽略 `Create` 却不能忽略 `Remove`？

**参考答案**：两者信息与职责不对称。`Create` 只带 lineage 哈希，无法直接构造路由树节点（缺 u64 键和父链接），而封块点的 `take_newly_registered_blocks` 能产出完整四元组——store 语义有更好的来源，Create 是「发射策略关不掉的噪声」。`Remove` 则没有替代来源：逐出发生在池内部深处（LRU 分配时的隐性弹最旧、`evict_inactive` 冲刷），只有 RAII 附件能在那个时刻发出信号——摘除语义只能靠它。

**练习 2**：假设消费者线程每 10 步才排一次水（而不是每步），风险模型里的哪个不等式被收紧了？最坏后果是什么？

**参考答案**：安全条件从 \( E_{\text{step}} \le C \) 变成 \( E_{10\,\text{step}} \le C \)——需要缓冲的事件量放大了约 10 倍，余量从数十倍缩到几倍，突发场景（冷冲刷 + 大 prefill 叠加）就可能越界触发 `Lagged`。最坏后果是前缀树永久失步且无告警（除非消费者显式检查 Lagged）：路由器持续基于幻觉调度。这正是常量注释强调「the scheduler drains it every step」的原因——每步排水把暴露窗口压到最小。

**练习 3**：一个部署里既想开 KV offload（u3-l1）又想开事件流做路由，行不行？

**参考答案**：以当前实现不行，至少不能天真地组合。4.3 讲过光标的「GPU-resident reuse」假设：事件流的世界里，命中块被默认为「从未离开 GPU、store 事件仍有效」；offload 的世界里块会经 CPU 层往返，逐出/恢复的 Remove/重注册节奏会与路由树脱节（恢复路径 `commit_loaded_blocks` 也不经过 `RequestKv` 的光标）。源码用注释显式记录了这个边界（「which holds wherever the event feed is enabled」）——两个 opt-in 各服务一类部署，交界处的语义是留给未来的工作。
